component.name: TuxTalk
component.summary: Hold a key, talk, and your words are typed for you

description.p: TuxTalk (formerly TalkType) is free voice dictation for Linux. Hold F8 and talk, let go, and your words are typed wherever your cursor is, in any app. Or tap F9 to start and tap again to stop. It works on Wayland and X11, on GNOME, KDE, Sway, Hyprland and more.
Everything runs on your own computer. Nothing you say is sent anywhere, and after the first download it works with no internet at all.

ul.li: NVIDIA's Parakeet by default, fast even without a graphics card, for English and 24 European languages
OpenAI's Whisper for 99 languages, from Tiny up to Large-v3
Any graphics card through Vulkan (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel), or CUDA on NVIDIA
First run picks a setup for your computer and language
Voice commands for punctuation, new lines and undo, plus your own phrases
Optional AI corrections, also on your computer: "three o'clock, no wait, four" types "four o'clock"
Fix a Word teaches it names and terms it keeps getting wrong
Hands-free mode that stops by itself when you go quiet
Back up your settings and load them on another computer
Your dictation stats and how much typing time you saved

screenshot.caption: Hold a key and talk: your words are typed into any app
First run recommends the best setup for your computer and language

description.p: TalkType is now TuxTalk, with voice editing and Your Words

ul.li: New name, same app. Settings, models, voice commands, stats and backups move over on their own
Voice editing (TuxTalk Labs): select text, hold Shift+F8 and say how to change it
Your Words: the names and terms you use come out spelled your way
Ctrl+Alt+P types your last dictation again, wherever your cursor is
Music and videos pause while you dictate
The recording indicator can follow the window you're dictating into (TuxTalk Labs)
Swiss German spelling: ss instead of ß
Preferences asks before closing with changes you didn't apply

description.p: Settings backup, and CUDA where you'd look for it

ul.li: The first run screen recommends a setup and asks your language on every computer, not only on GNOME or with an NVIDIA card
Back up your settings, voice commands, Fix a Word words and stats to a file, and load it on another computer
TuxTalk keeps your last 10 settings, so a change or an update that went wrong can be undone
CUDA is listed under Device on NVIDIA computers, like Vulkan
Use Recommended and "What works with what?" in Preferences
A changed hotkey can be tested right away, and KDE's own shortcuts are pointed out
AI corrections understand "No, actually, make that four"
Hands-free stops after 10 seconds when nothing is said

description.p: Smarter corrections and spoken addresses

ul.li: Corrections handle saying the whole thing again ("scratch that, send it to Jim") and "actually" without a pause
Say an email or web address with "dot" and it's written as an address
Message boxes have rounded corners on KDE, like every other TuxTalk window
The welcome screen's hotkey test reads your keyboard directly

description.p: Clearer typing problems, faster start and better self-corrections

ul.li: When a dictation can't be typed, TuxTalk says why and what fixes it
Whisper models load once at start instead of twice
Self-corrections work when a pause splits off "no wait"
Performance has a Custom item that opens Preferences, in the GNOME menu too
Long dropdown lists open in columns; Stats and Updates fit the window
The welcome screen has a clear button to change language, model or graphics card
Emoji and language flags show in the AppImage on newer distros

description.p: Fixes for GNOME and KDE

ul.li: Dropdowns work on a second monitor under GNOME on Wayland, and open cleanly on KDE
Ordinary sentences are no longer turned into email addresses
Windows show TuxTalk's icon on KDE instead of a generic one
Preferences highlights the tab it opened on
Choosing the Performance preset already in use no longer restarts the service
Current screenshots

description.p: A recommended setup for your computer

ul.li: First run shows one recommended setup for your graphics card and language, with other options explained
AMD and Intel graphics are used at first run through Vulkan, after a speed check
Parakeet is the default model for new installs
Three Performance presets: Recommended for this computer, Lightest and Battery saver
Existing users are told once if there's a better setup for their computer
The menus show what really runs, and large-v3 on Vulkan no longer runs as medium
A dictation that doesn't reach the window is reported instead of lost silently

description.p: Keyboard layout and hotkey fixes

ul.li: Typing mode uses the real keys of non-US layouts, so Y and Z and accented letters come out right
On X11 the active keyboard layout is used, not the first one in the list
Text a layout can't type is pasted instead, on X11 too
The hotkey no longer leaks into the focused app on KDE and GNOME
Dictations stay out of clipboard manager history, with an option to restore the clipboard

description.p: Parakeet on the graphics card, and terminal dictation on more desktops

ul.li: Parakeet runs on the graphics card through Vulkan, about 10 times faster
Terminal paste works on Sway, i3, Hyprland, niri and X11 desktops like XFCE, MATE and Cinnamon
Ghostty, GNOME Console, Guake and other terminals get the right paste
OK closes Preferences again when the device is Vulkan
A quick accidental tap of the key no longer types a stray word
Help links to the TuxTalk Discussions page

description.p: Performance presets work with Vulkan

ul.li: Most Accurate can be set up through Vulkan on NVIDIA, AMD and Intel graphics
Graphics presets keep you on Vulkan instead of switching to the processor

description.p: A lighter way to use an NVIDIA graphics card

ul.li: NVIDIA cards can now use the 24 MB Vulkan engine instead of the 1.4 GB CUDA libraries, at about the same speed
First-run setup offers a choice between Full (CUDA) and Light (Vulkan)
The Large model can be set up through Vulkan on NVIDIA, AMD and Intel graphics

description.p: Usage stats, and Whisper on AMD and Intel graphics

ul.li: Whisper models can now use AMD and Intel graphics, after a quick check that it's actually faster
See how many words you have dictated today, this week and all time, and how much typing time it saved
A chart of the last two weeks, and how your dictation speed compares with your typing speed
Only the numbers are kept, on your computer, never what you said

description.p: Bug fixes

ul.li: Launch at login is repaired if it still points at an old downloaded AppImage
The GNOME panel menu keeps working when TuxTalk's tray restarts

description.p: The AppImage can now be updated by AppImageUpdate and similar tools
Teach TuxTalk words it keeps getting wrong

ul.li: Fix a Word: pick a misheard word from a recent dictation and type the right spelling, and it's fixed in every dictation from then on
Preferences comes to the front if it's already open behind another window
Saving Preferences no longer removes a voice command added while it was open
Larger, easier to read text in Preferences

description.p: Works without PortAudio installed

ul.li: Bundles PortAudio as a fallback, so the microphone works on systems without it

description.p: The AppImage starts on more systems

ul.li: No longer needs libfuse2, so it runs on Ubuntu 26.04 and other systems without it
Bundles the tray icon library, so a system without it no longer crashes on launch

description.p: Bug fixes

ul.li: Fixed the dictation key sometimes staying stuck down in VM windows, remote desktops and games
Launch at login now uses the installed AppImage, not the copy in Downloads
The Device line shows CPU when using Parakeet
The AI cleanup engine no longer keeps running after TuxTalk closes

description.p: Optional hands-free dictation

ul.li: Double-tap the toggle key and the recording stops by itself when you stop talking
A single tap is still a normal on/off toggle
Fixed the Flatpak toggle shortcut sometimes needing two presses after a recording ended

description.p: Optional dictation cleanup and startup download fixes

ul.li: Remove "um", "uh" and accidentally repeated words, with nothing to download
Optional local AI fixes self-corrections, with every edit checked before it is typed
Cancelling a model download at startup is respected and falls back to a model you already have
Fixed a crash after downloading a model at startup
Tray presets and injection modes no longer restart dictation twice

description.p: New optional Parakeet speech model and a Recent Dictations menu

ul.li: NVIDIA Parakeet: accuracy close to Whisper large-v3, fast on an ordinary processor, English and 24 European languages
New "Fast and Accurate" performance preset
Recent Dictations menu: re-copy your last 20 dictations, kept in memory only

description.p: Dictation into a terminal now works on KDE

ul.li: Text dictated into a terminal actually appears - it previously did nothing at all
"new line" and "new paragraph" work inside a terminal
Dictating into Claude Desktop is more reliable on KDE
Terminal recognition no longer depends on exact capitalisation

description.p: Settings that said they were applied now actually are

ul.li: Changing your hotkey takes effect immediately again
Custom voice commands apply on the next dictation, with no restart
Switching microphone actually switches microphone
Commands containing a number match either spelling ("one" or "1")
Cancelling a model download no longer leaves the wrong model saved
Ready for GNOME 51

description.p: Preferences polish

ul.li: The recording-indicator color picker now shows a visible checkmark on white and other light-colored swatches
Scrolling a Preferences or setup window no longer stalls when the pointer is over a dropdown
Clearer wording for how .deb/.rpm installs update themselves

description.p: Fixes how TuxTalk updates itself, so updating works correctly however you installed it

ul.li: .deb / .rpm installs now update through your package manager in one click (with a password prompt) instead of failing on a missing FUSE library
Arch (AUR) installs are pointed to the AUR helper; AppImage installs keep updating in place
"Check for Updates" shows one clear window; the GNOME panel and system-tray menus behave identically
TuxTalk now reliably restarts after an update
About, Help and Voice Commands windows now always open, and are no longer hidden behind the update window

description.p: Native .deb and .rpm packages, a smaller download, and a first run that just works

ul.li: New .deb (Debian/Ubuntu/Mint) and .rpm (Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE) packages
Download nearly halved (306 MB to 135 MB) by removing an unused library
Launches at login after setup; restart reminder moved to the end of setup
Fixed startup, hotkeys and permission checks on Fedora; many first-run fixes

description.p: Polished first-run experience with improved UX

ul.li: Simple modal dialog for hotkey changes (not full Preferences window)
Loop-back verification: after changing keys, immediately verify new keys
Progress dialog when downloading Whisper models
Fixed dialog timing: welcome screen now appears before hotkey verification
First run only marked complete after successful hotkey verification

description.p: Bug fixes and improvements

ul.li: Fixed 'new line' voice command
Optimized AppImage size
